title: Pending orders: limits and stops

inOneLine.simple: A pending order waits for price to reach your level. Limits buy lower or sell higher. Stops buy higher or sell lower.
inOneLine.balanced: [[pending-order|Pending orders]]: buy limit below price, sell limit above, buy stop above, sell stop below. Nothing happens unless price reaches the level.

explain.simple: You do not have to trade now. A pending order waits. A buy limit sits below the current price: you want to buy cheaper. A sell limit sits above: you want to sell higher. A buy stop sits above the current price: you want to buy only if price rises to that level. A sell stop sits below: you want to sell only if price falls to that level. If price never gets there, no trade opens.
explain.balanced: In MetaTrader, buy pending orders are triggered by the [[ask]] and sell pending orders by the [[bid]]. A [[limit-order]] aims for your price or better. A [[stop-order]] becomes a market order once triggered, so it can fill worse than its level, especially in fast markets or [[gap|gaps]]. Many brokers set a minimum distance between the current price and a pending order, and you can usually add a stop loss and take profit when you place it.

steps: Buy limit at 1.09500: below the ask. Triggers if the ask falls to 1.09500.
Sell limit at 1.10500: above the bid. Triggers if the bid rises to 1.10500.
Buy stop at 1.10500: above the ask. Triggers if the ask rises to 1.10500.
Sell stop at 1.09500: below the bid. Triggers if the bid falls to 1.09500.

assumptions: A buy stop on EUR/USD at 1.10500, for a possible breakout
steps: Price rises quickly and the ask jumps from 1.10490 to 1.10520.
The order triggers and becomes a market order.
It fills at 1.10520, 2 pips above the level.
That slippage costs 2 × 1 USD = 2 USD compared with the planned price.

explainSimpler: Limit: 'get me a better price than now.' Stop: 'only get me in if price moves past this point.'
commonMistake: Mixing up limit and stop orders. Putting a buy limit above the current price, or a buy stop below it, is the wrong way round. The platform will usually reject it, or you may end up placing an order you did not intend.

quickCheck.prompt: EUR/USD ask is 1.10000. You want to buy only if price drops to 1.09700. Which order?

options.explanation: Right: a buy limit sits below the current price.
No: a buy stop sits above the current price.
No: that would open a sell, and a sell limit sits above the price.

quickCheck.prompt: Where does a sell stop go?

options.explanation: Right: a sell stop triggers if price falls to the level.
No: a sell order above the price is a sell limit.

quickCheck.prompt: A pending order's price is never reached. What happens?

options.explanation: Right: a pending order only opens a trade if price reaches its level.

options.text: It fills at the end of the day anyway
options.explanation: No: it waits until it triggers, expires, or you delete it.

doItNow.instructions: On your demo account, place a buy limit on EUR/USD below the current price, with a stop loss and take profit. Check it in the Trade tab, then delete it. Follow the task card.
